elaine: Heads-up — after the 12:28 deploy I can't find traces for batch-worker-v2. Logs look fine but spans are missing (only root operation shows). Anyone seen this pattern?

sam: Are you seeing the requests show up in metrics? If metrics are fine but traces are gone it could be sampler or service name mismatch. Which collector/agent is the app pointing to?

elaine: Metrics are normal, throughput unchanged. We send to otlp-collector.redwood.internal:4317. Example header from request: traceparent present in logs for one trace id: 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736. But when I paste that into Jaeger nothing shows up.

mike: Quick checklist: 1) confirm OTEL_SERVICE_NAME in container, 2) check OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, 3) verify Collector ingestion logs for that traceid. You can curl the collector health:

```bash
curl -sS http://otlp-collector.redwood.internal:13133/healthz
```

nina: Also check if the instrumentation is actually flushing. We had a similar thing where batch job exited before exporter flushed. For SDKs that can happen with batch span processor if process exits quickly.

ashley: FYI we upgraded the opentelemetry-java SDK on that image last week — there was an unrelated PR that changed the default sampler behavior for SDK v1.22. If the sampler became probabilistic it could drop low-volume async spans.

sam: Good catch. Could be sampler or the service name the collector expects. In collector we filter by resource.service.name for the dashboard. Try running this on a worker to dump resource attrs:

```bash
# inside container
python -c "from opentelemetry import trace; print(trace.get_tracer_provider().resource.attributes)"
```

mike: If you want a fast trace lookup you can query the collector logs for the traceid too:

```bash
jq -r 'select(.body|test("4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736"))' /var/log/otel-collector/collector.log | tail -n 50
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Successfully rolled batch-worker-v2 image tag canary-2026-03-16 to cluster/staging :rocket:

elaine: I grepped the collector logs and I see the traceid coming in but the resource.service.name is "batch_worker" (underscore) while our dashboards expect "batch-worker-v2" (dash). That explains why Jaeger didn't surface it under the service view.

nina: Ah that fits. Collector-side join/aggregation rules treat those as separate services so the dashboard tile won't pick up the underscore name. Two fixes: change OTEL_SERVICE_NAME in the container to match the dashboard, or update the dashboard/collector processing to normalize names.

ashley: For a quick fix set env vars in the deployment: "OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=batch-worker-v2" and restart. Also confirm sampler settings: set OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=traceidratio and OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.05 if you want ~5% sampling consistently until we audit config.

sam: Another helpful check — look for the span names for the child operations. If you see only the root span in Jaeger it might be that child spans are being created but not ended due to missing try/finally or Context propagation broken across threads. For Java check MDC vs Context propagation when using executor services.

elaine: I patched the deployment to set OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=batch-worker-v2 and restarted one canary pod. I can now see the same traceid in Jaeger and I can expand child spans. Looks like the name mismatch was the main culprit. Thanks all! :tada:

mike: Nice. If you want I can open a small infra task to add a linter that ensures service name matches our naming convention in the docker image build.

elaine: Please do. Also will file a follow-up to check SDK upgrade notes and sampler defaults.

ashley: Linking internal docs for folks who hit this: https://wiki.redwood/internal/observability/tracing#service-names-and-sampling

elaine: closing loop — resolved in canary, rolling to prod after canary passes. Thanks. :thumbsup:
